Why read Oziewicz this way?

In memoriam · Zbigniew Oziewicz, 1941–2020

“Science is subjective.”
“Only a controversial subject is interesting.”
“Everybody has a right to be right.”

His talk to the Natural Philosophy Alliance, 2009 (in the repository, in his own voice); Science must never be objective and Are peer reviewers Guardians of the Truth?, 2013.

How the notes keep faith with it

  1. State each claim in its strongest form before testing it.
  2. Check the mathematics, not allegiance: does the identity hold, does the construction compose, does the statement follow?
  3. Report the result either way: textbook physics in new notation, or a conflict that survives.

Where the method parts from him

He held that science needs no criterion for who is right. A repository that checks derivations does not share that view, and it does not claim that he would have agreed with it.

House rules

  • A statement of what a paper says is a reading, keyed to its equation numbers, not a quotation.
  • checked means a mathematical step was reproduced by computer algebra. It does not mean Oziewicz was right, or that the reading is faithful.
  • Each note says what it inherits from earlier notes and what it retracts.
  • Drafted with Claude (Anthropic). I review and merge every change. No external peer review.
  • I co-authored one of the papers read here. That is a relationship, not independence.

Oziewicz project · From Grassmann to Clifford · 3 / 23

The ladder so far: relativity with bodies first

StepQuestionFinding
1What does the mass centre of Many-body mass-centre (2014; long version 2017) define?Standard special relativity in a coordinate-free notation: the mass centre is the centre-of-momentum frame.
2Can the mass centre be the third observer of his ternary velocity? (Beyond what he published.)For two bodies, yes. For three or more, no Lorentz link can depend on the pair alone, carry one body to the other and compose. This part of his “astonishing conflict” survives.
3What is left below the metric, with a body as a process and a clock?Velocity, its non-reciprocity and the mass centre survive. His symmetric gamma is the metric itself. His clock is a connection, not a time.
4How are a clock's vorticity, spin and the centre related?A correction to step 1: a covariant centre worldline exists. Each clock picks its own centre, and the spin is P ∧ L.

No step yet departs from standard relativity or predicts anything new. What is his own is the presentation, several of the results, and the questions.

Today's example: From Grassmann to Clifford (1986)

The thesis in three claims

  1. Exterior multiplication e and its transpose i are fermion creation and annihilation operators, with no metric: .
  2. A Clifford generator is a “quasi-particle”: , a creator plus an annihilator.
  3. The Clifford product lives on the same space as the Grassmann algebra. The map from vectors to covectors need not be symmetric: .

Read alongside

Oziewicz 1997, Clifford algebra of multivectors: his own sequel

Jadczyk 2021, On the bundle of Clifford algebras over the space of quadratic forms, dedicated to his memory

Sobczyk 2023–2026: geometric algebras built from null vectors

Where the talk ends up

What is given without any choice is the evaluation of a covector on a vector. The Grassmann algebra is its Fock space. A metric is the choice of a subspace: the graph of .

Z. Oziewicz, in J. S. R. Chisholm and A. K. Common (eds.), Clifford Algebras and Their Applications in Mathematical Physics, NATO ASI C 183, Reidel 1986, pp. 245–255.

Oziewicz project · From Grassmann to Clifford · 5 / 23

Two spaces, neither first

A covector is its kernel plus one vector on which it reads 1. Its value is the number of sheets the arrow pierces: no length, no angle.

A metric identifies L with L* and hides the difference. The paper insists that not choosing a metric is not the same as having none available.

Figure from the supplement, §3.1; its numbers (, and 4 fronts crossed) are checked exactly before it is drawn. Panel (c) draws an exact form.

Oziewicz project · From Grassmann to Clifford · 19 / 23

The thesis: three verdicts

1 · Proved

For every linear , the Grassmann space with carries an associative product. Postulated in 1986, constructed by Oziewicz in 1997, proved in full by Chevalley, Bourbaki and Jadczyk, checked here for generic .

2 · Reduced

Only the symmetric part determines the algebra. is a gauge that chooses the grading. So is over-parametrised, and Oziewicz says so himself in 1997.

3 · Not a theorem

“Primary” is a claim of priority: one can start from Clifford and get Grassmann as . What can be defended: the abstract Clifford algebra does not know what a bivector is. The pair (algebra, grading) does, and the Grassmann structure is that extra datum.

The thesis in its sharper form

What is given without any choice is the evaluation of covectors on vectors. The Grassmann algebra is its Fock space. A metric is the choice of a subspace, the graph of , to which evaluation is restricted.

Also corrected: the 1986 “symplectic Clifford algebra” () is the Grassmann algebra again, not the Weyl algebra, which deforms the symmetric algebra. 1997 puts it there.

Open questions

Fields, not points

In 1986 , and are fields; evaluation is the same at every point. Is the natural setting the doubled bundle , with and a field of graphs, and the obstruction in §9?

The symmetric twin

Permanents in place of determinants in (3), commutators in (16): does the same construction give the Weyl algebra, with the roles of and exchanged?

The null substrate

Is the simplex metric of local duality singled out by anything in the evaluation structure, or only by its symmetry? Does anything in the programme depend on ?

Braids

1997 allows any pre-braid. Is still an isometry of a braided doubled space? Is still a sum of commuting operators with two eigenvalues each?

And one for the literature: where is Conjecture 8.2 already known? The Fierz identities are the place to look.

An invitation

How you can help

  1. Read an original against its reading. Every note links to the paper, in references/bibliography.md.
  2. Run a check, or break one. Each note has its script in src/.
  3. Disagree in the open. Open an issue on GitHub. A disagreement is recorded the way a result is.
  4. Suggest what to read next, and which of his drafts deserve a summary.
